sentences.text: Butyricimonas faecihominis was described from strain 180-3, one of two strains isolated from human faeces that were obligately anaerobic, non-pigmented, non-spore-forming, non-motile, Gram-stain-negative rods.
Those strains produced butyric and isobutyric acids as end products from glucose, and their growth was inhibited on medium containing 20 percent bile.
A strain of Butyricimonas faecihominis, described as a butyrate-producing bacterium, was isolated from feces of a Japanese Alzheimer's disease patient.
A case report identified Butyricimonas faecihominis, described as a rarely reported pathogen, from blood cultures of a 50-year-old man whose perianal abscess progressed to septic shock.
